content.user_title: Design Apple Status and Progress Interfaces
content.value_statement: Unclear progress and status feedback can make Apple platform interfaces feel stalled or inconsistent. This skill applies Apple HIG guidance to indicators, status bars, and Activity rings.
actual_capabilities: Recommends determinate or indeterminate progress indicators based on task duration and measurability.
Reviews indicator placement, movement, labels, cancellation controls, and completion transitions.
Evaluates status bar visibility, readability, safe-area handling, and immersive presentation behavior.
Checks Activity ring use against Apple Fitness purpose, color, margin, labeling, and ownership rules.
Provides platform-specific guidance for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS where supported.
Structures recommendations around rationale, timing, animation, accessibility, and platform behavior.
limitations: The skill provides design guidance and does not implement or test production interfaces.
Recommendations depend on accurate task duration, platform, context, and user-flow details.
Activity rings are limited to Move, Exercise, and Stand data for one person.
Apple guidance can change, so teams should verify final decisions against current official documentation.

use_cases.title: Choose Loading Feedback
use_cases.description: Select an appropriate indicator and behavior for downloads, uploads, refreshes, or other waiting states.

use_cases.title: Review Apple Platform UI
use_cases.description: Audit status bars and progress states for clarity, consistency, safe-area handling, and platform conventions.

use_cases.title: Validate Fitness Displays
use_cases.description: Check Activity ring usage, appearance, data meaning, and platform support before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Indicator
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose a progress indicator for [operation]. Its duration is [known or unknown], it usually takes [time], and the target platform is [platform].
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a basic recommendation for one operation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Progress Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my [screen or flow] for progress feedback. Recommend indicator type, placement, labels, cancellation behavior, and completion transitions for [platform].
prompt_templates.scenario: A designer wants a structured review of an existing flow.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Status Bar
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this status bar design for [iOS or iPadOS]. Check readability, content overlap, visibility, immersive transitions, and restoration behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs focused guidance for status bar behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Fitness Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an HIG review for this [health or fitness app] across [platforms]. Evaluate Activity ring purpose, ownership, color, margins, labels, notifications, and accessibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs a cross-platform Activity ring audit.

output_examples.input: A file export takes about 30 seconds, and the app can measure completed items.
output_examples.output: Use a determinate progress bar near the export content. Report accurate advancement, keep it moving, and offer cancellation when interruption is safe.

output_examples.input: An iPhone gallery hides the status bar during full-screen viewing.
output_examples.output: Temporary hiding is appropriate for immersive media. Restore the status bar with a simple gesture and keep underlying controls outside its interaction area.

output_examples.input: A meditation app uses red, green, and blue rings to show breathing goals.
output_examples.output: Do not use Activity rings for breathing goals. Choose a distinct visualization because Apple reserves this design for Move, Exercise, and Stand progress.

best_practices: Provide the target platform, expected duration, and whether progress can be measured.
Describe cancellation consequences and any transition from unknown to known progress.
Include screenshots or flow details when requesting layout, readability, or placement guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not request a determinate percentage when the operation cannot measure real progress.
Do not use multiple competing indicators for one operation or place feedback far from affected content.
Do not repurpose Activity rings for unrelated metrics, decoration, branding, or multiple people.

faq.question: When should I use a determinate progress indicator?
faq.answer: Use one when the operation has measurable advancement or a well-defined duration.

faq.question: When is a spinner appropriate?
faq.answer: Use a spinner when duration is unknown, for compact spaces, or for asynchronous background work.

faq.question: Can an indicator change from indeterminate to determinate?
faq.answer: Yes. Switch when reliable progress becomes available, but avoid changing from a circular shape to a bar.

faq.question: Should users be able to cancel an operation?
faq.answer: Offer cancellation when interruption is safe. Explain lost progress or other consequences before stopping destructive operations.

faq.question: When can an app hide the status bar?
faq.answer: Hide it temporarily for immersive content, then provide a simple way to restore it.

faq.question: Can Activity rings represent custom goals?
faq.answer: No. Activity rings are reserved for one person's Move, Exercise, and Stand progress.
